title: Crankshaft / Camshaft Position Correlation Bank 1 Sensor B
shortDescription: Bank 1 exhaust cam timing out of correlation with crank.
fullDescription:
P0017 sets when the cam-position signal does not correlate with crank position within the calibrated window. Causes range from a stretched timing chain to a stuck VVT solenoid or low oil pressure.

Ignoring chain wear is risky on interference engines; investigate immediately if there is a startup rattle.
safetyImpact: Possible engine damage if a chain skips - investigate promptly.

fixSteps.title: Read cam advance PIDs
fixSteps.instruction: Compare commanded vs actual at varying RPM.

fixSteps.title: Inspect chain
fixSteps.instruction: Use the manual to verify stretch with a load tool.

fixSteps.title: Replace failed component
fixSteps.instruction: Solenoid, phaser, or chain set as indicated.

faq.a: Only short distances - chain failure is catastrophic.
On some engines yes - dirty oil sticks VVT.

title: Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Circuit: circuit malfunction.
fullDescription:
P0070 sets when the circuit malfunction circuit reports a fault. The ECM uses ambient temperature for cold-start and HVAC strategies; an out-of-range reading skews fueling and warm-up timing.

Verify wiring, then bench-test or substitute the component to confirm.
safetyImpact: Reduced power and economy; not unsafe in the short term.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Look for green crust / pin damage.

title: Insufficient Coolant Temperature for Closed Loop Fuel Control
shortDescription: Coolant has not reached closed-loop threshold within the expected time.
fullDescription:
P0125 sets when the engine cannot reach the coolant temperature required for closed-loop fueling within a calibrated drive time.

A stuck-open thermostat is the dominant cause; verify with a scan tool that ECT actually rises to ~190F. Closed-loop fueling is what manages emissions, so the MIL stays on until corrected.
safetyImpact: Worse fuel economy and emissions; not unsafe.

fixSteps.title: Verify ECT sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Compare to IR temp at engine.

faq.a: Yes - cold airflow keeps coolant below threshold.

title: Coolant Temperature Below Thermostat Regulating Temperature
shortDescription: Coolant is below the thermostat's regulating point during steady operation.
fullDescription:
P0128 specifically calls out a thermostat that is opening too early or stuck open. Different from P0125 in that it monitors the regulating set-point during cruise.

Replacement of the thermostat almost always clears it. Make sure the new unit is OE-temperature spec.
safetyImpact: Mild fuel economy/emissions impact only.

faq.a: P0128 is steady-state; P0125 is warm-up time.
Usually - air pockets cause repeat codes.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
shortDescription: O2 Sensor Circuit (Bank 1, Sensor 1): general circuit fault.
fullDescription:
P0130 sets when the bank-1 oxygen sensor reports general circuit fault. Pre-CAT sensors directly drive fuel trim, so a bad signal causes rich/lean issues.

Most common fix is replacing the sensor with an OE-quality part. Avoid generic units on modern engines.
safetyImpact: Failed emissions and possible drivability problems.

faq.a: Sensor 1 is pre, Sensor 2 is post.

title: System Too Lean Bank 1
shortDescription: Long-term fuel trim is biased lean on bank 1.
fullDescription:
P0171 sets when long-term fuel trim on bank 1 exceeds the calibrated lean threshold. The ECM has been adding/removing fuel beyond the normal correction window.

Diagnose using a smoke test (lean) or fuel-pressure check (rich) before replacing parts.
safetyImpact: Long-term lean conditions can damage the catalyst; address promptly.

fixSteps.title: Read fuel-trim PIDs
fixSteps.instruction: Compare STFT and LTFT at idle and cruise.

fixSteps.title: Check fuel pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Compare to spec at idle and WOT.

faq.a: Yes briefly, but lean conditions risk catalyst damage.
Yes - it's the fastest diagnostic for lean.
